analysis:
Examined the ProviderLoop.swift head text (lines 1-1220) and the DaemonState+Coding.swift patch. ProviderLoop.swift adds three pieces of actor state: selectedModelRecovery (line 726), selectedModelRecoveryLoadOverride (line 728, nil in production, test seam) and enabledModelsAtLastSwitch (line 735). It also adds savedEnabledModels (line 731), seeded from config.config.backend.enabledModels in init (line 897). These are in-memory bookkeeping fields. The visible changes do not touch the coordinator WebSocket contract (TB-002), key handling (A-003), attestation (TB-009/TB-011), the add-on hold socket (TB-012) or the SSD prefix cache (T-041).

DaemonState+Coding.swift adds CodingKeys and decodeIfPresent entries for enabledModelsAtStart, enabledModelsAtLastSwitch and selectedModelRecovery. Decoding is optional, so older state files remain readable. The state file holds model IDs and recovery entries, not prompts or keys. The patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not see the encode side or the new SelectedModelRecoveryEntry type. I assume they expose only model IDs and statuses; this is not confirmed.

Remaining integration questions for the next pass:
- Does ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift, which is not in the supplied batch, reload models only through the existing admission, memory and slot-cap gates, and does it avoid eviction as its comment claims?
- Does the recovery path respect lifecycle draining, update phases and retirement tombstones (retiringModels, failedSelfTestHashes), so a model retired after a failed self-test cannot be reloaded?
- Does the policy refresh that updates savedEnabledModels read the config file safely, and does it avoid changing the serving set outside a committed switch?
- Do the daemon-state additions leak anything beyond model IDs?
No concrete regression is identified from the supplied evidence.
